title: Constructibility of fibre-assassin containment for schemes over an affine base
statement: Let $g:T\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $B$ affine. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation: locally it has an exact presentation $\mathcal O_T^r\to\mathcal O_T^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Let $H\subseteq T$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $H\to B$ is quasi-compact. Use scheme-theoretic fibres and tensor pullback [def-trf-relative-assassin, def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\{b\in B\mid\operatorname{Ass}_{T_b}(F_b)\subseteq |H_b|\}$ is a constructible subset of $|B|$ [def-weil-constructible-subset].

source.place: Tag 05KR (lemma-relative-assassin-constructible), restricted to affine base, exactly the affine reduction in its proof.

proof.text: Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], the spectra $B_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$ have affine transitions and limit $B$. This is a small nonempty directed set: its elements are subrings of the set $A$, the image of $\mathbf Z$ is one, and the subring generated by the union of two finite generating sets is an upper bound. The $B_i$ are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The case $n=0$ of [lem-trf-mvpolynomial-noetherian] makes $\mathbf Z$ Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] therefore makes every $A_i$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05KR (lemma-relative-assassin-constructible), first paragraph: directed finite-type integer-subalgebra approximation; Noetherianity uses Algebra Tag 00FN.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-family-descent] to the singleton family $T\to B$, obtaining a finitely presented qcqs model $T_i\to B_i$ with $T\cong T_i\times_{B_i}B$. For $j\geq i$ put $T_j=T_i\times_{B_i}B_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], these models remain finitely presented and qcqs. Their transitions are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]: they are base changes of the affine maps $B_k\to B_j$. The limit is $T$: apply [lem-kun-fibre-product-limits] to the constant systems $T_i,B_i$ and the system $B_j$. The constant systems have the indicated limits because a compatible cone over a nonempty directed poset has identical components. Thus $T=\varprojlim_{j\geq i}T_j$ with affine transitions.

source.place: Tag 05KR, first paragraph: scheme descent by Limits Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); Limits Tag 01YZ (lemma-scheme-over-limit), whose limit assertion is also the cited general fibre-product limit theorem.

proof.text: Since $H\to B$ is quasi-compact and $B$ affine, $H$ is quasi-compact by the definition of a quasi-compact morphism in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] to the limit $T=\varprojlim T_j$: at a later index $k$ there is an open $H_k\subseteq T_k$ with inverse image $H$. Now apply clause (1) of [lem-pc-fp-module-map-descent] to $T_k\to\operatorname{Spec}A_k$ and its base changes. All base rings are Noetherian by Step 1, so its hypotheses hold. At a later index $l$ it gives a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $F_l$ pulling back to $F$. Put $H_l$ equal to the inverse image of $H_k$. Replace $i$ by $l$. We now have $(T,F,H)$ as the base change of $(T_i,F_i,H_i)$ over the Noetherian affine base $B_i$. No quasi-compactness of $H_i\to B_i$ is needed in the generic-point argument below.

source.place: Tag 05KR, first paragraph: descent of the module by Limits Tag 01ZR (lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation) and the open by Tag 01Z4 (lemma-descend-opens), in the opposite order to avoid reindexing an already descended module.

proof.text: Let $E_i=\{b_i\in B_i\mid\operatorname{Ass}_{(T_i)_{b_i}}((F_i)_{b_i})\subseteq |(H_i)_{b_i}|\}$ and let $p_i:B\to B_i$ be the projection. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-fibre-assassin-containment-base-change] hold: finite presentation of $T_i\to B_i$ implies locally finite type, and the local finite presentation of $F_i$ includes a finite generating surjection. Applying that node point by point gives the exact equality $E=p_i^{-1}(E_i)$, with no flatness assumption on $p_i$.

source.place: Tag 05KR, first paragraph: reduction via Tag 05KQ (lemma-base-change-assassin-in-U).

proof.text: Fix a nonempty irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq |B_i|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $Z=V(\mathfrak p)$ for a prime $\mathfrak p\subset A_i$. Give it its reduced closed-scheme structure $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i/\mathfrak p)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The zero prime is a generic point of this scheme by the closure formula in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. Form $(T_Z,F_Z,H_Z)$ by base change to $Z$. The morphism $T_Z\to Z$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], hence finite type. The module $F_Z$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and finitely presented by [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation], hence of finite type. The containment locus of this triple is precisely $E_i\cap Z$ by [lem-sfb-fibre-assassin-containment-base-change].

source.place: Tag 05KR, final paragraph: base change to an irreducible closed subscheme; supporting Tags 01J3 (reduced induced structure), 01TP (finite presentation), 01BG and 01BQ (module pullback).

proof.text: If the generic fibre of the triple over $Z$ has all its associated points in $H_Z$, [lem-sfb-generic-fibre-assassin-containment-spreads] gives a nonempty open $V\subseteq Z$ contained in $E_i\cap Z$. If it does not, [lem-sfb-generic-fibre-assassin-noncontainment-spreads] gives a nonempty open $V\subseteq Z$ disjoint from $E_i\cap Z$. Step 5 verified finite type of the morphism and module and irreducibility of the base, exactly the hypotheses of both nodes; neither requires flatness. Thus every irreducible closed subset has the alternative required by [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion]. Its finite affine Noetherian-cover hypothesis is satisfied by the single chart $B_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. It follows that $E_i$ is constructible.

source.place: Tag 05KR, final paragraph: Tags 05KP (lemma-good-case), 05KN (lemma-bad-case) and Topology Tag 053Z (lemma-characterize-constructible-Noetherian).

proof.text: By [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], the inverse image $p_i^{-1}(E_i)$ is constructible under the arbitrary scheme morphism $p_i:B\to B_i$. By Step 4 this inverse image is $E$, proving the assertion. If $B$ is empty, the conclusion also follows directly since $E=\varnothing$ is constructible.

source.place: Tag 05KR, first paragraph: pulling back the Noetherian-model locus; Morphisms Tag 054I (lemma-inverse-image-constructible).
